- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml: lines 796-811 (the `claude_fixer_awaiting_session` check) interacting with line 1104 (the deterministic-skip condition) | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `claude_fixer_awaiting_session` check is gated on `[ "${EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]`, so a `pull_request` event (e.g., `synchronize`) with a hand-off comment whose SHA matches the new head SHA can fall through to the deterministic-skip block, bypassing the pending findings.
  WHY: In the edge case where a `synchronize` event lands on the same head SHA (force-push of identical content, or any same-SHA push GitHub still emits `synchronize` for), the hand-off comment's `<!-- ai:claude-fixer-handoff:v1 kind=findings head=<sha> round=N -->` matches the current `pr_head_sha_gate`, but the awaiting-session branch is skipped because the event is `pull_request`, not `workflow_dispatch`. SHOULD_RUN stays "true" and the doc-only/small-diff route fires — findings are never re-handed-off, and `deterministic-skip-merge` enables auto-merge on the head. The reviewer notes this is consistent with the PR description's stated intent ("the next push is evaluated for the skip") and is flagging it as a documented assumption rather than a defect.
- Requirement: Clarify that a Claude session must fix only a `claude/*` PR that does not auto-merge via the deterministic skip or a clean review.
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md lines 1882-1891
  Evidence of absence: The added sentence "A `claude/*` PR that qualifies for the deterministic doc-only or small-diff skip takes it like any other PR ... So a Claude session must fix these PRs" reads ambiguously. "These PRs" sits at the start of the new sentence, but the previous sentence just said the skip path applies to `claude/*` PRs that qualify. A reader could parse "these PRs" as referring to all `claude/*` PRs, which would contradict the auto-merge claim.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
